definition: Inept means lacking skill; not capable or qualified.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inept. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inept should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Two lessons in, Aldo remained an inept skater, towed around the rink by more forgiving friends.
An awkward first attempt wobbles but may find its feet; inept performance keeps failing the task outright.
Hopeless goes past inept — beyond training, beyond improvement, beyond hope.

Unskilled says only that training or practice is missing — an unskilled worker may do fine once taught. Inept passes a harder judgment: the ability itself is absent, so the attempt keeps failing no matter how long the person has worked at it.

Bungling describes botching a job in real time — the live spectacle of things going wrong in someone's hands. Inept is the standing verdict behind that spectacle: the skill was never there to begin with. A bungling moment can happen to anyone; an inept practitioner supplies such moments reliably.

commands the craft completely
Jorge booked the aptitude test for eight in the morning, on the theory that his nerves woke up at nine.
Inept means lacking skill; not capable or qualified.
The kingdom's most inept counterfeiter was arrested before lunch.

His banknotes spelled the realm's name two different ways — both wrong — priced themselves at "ten-ish crowns," and featured a king who looked, the constable testified, "like a potato in a crown." He had worked on them for a year.
Effort was never the problem.
Inept is the exact word because the counterfeiter is lacking skill — not capable or qualified — and no amount of trying fixes that by itself.
Clumsy would blame his hands; inexperienced would promise he'll improve.
Inept passes the harder judgment: the ability itself is missing.
The word applies wherever honest effort keeps producing failure.
Inept is the flat judgment that skill is absent — kinder than useless, harder than inexperienced.
Keep this unit's rudimentary beside it for comparison: rudimentary skill is real but undeveloped, a beginning; inept performance fails outright, however long it has practiced.
The beginner's Spanish is rudimentary; the guide who's been wrong about every date for ten years is inept.

The garden co-op elected Bert treasurer for the friendliest of reasons: he was the only member who raised a hand.
He took the bookkeeping workshop twice, bought the recommended software, and taped a checklist inside the ledger.
Still the dues sheet never balanced.
In March he paid the water bill twice; in April he recorded the plant sale as an expense.
By June even Bert admitted what the audit made plain: with numbers he was inept, and no amount of effort was turning that around.
The co-op thanked him, moved him to the seed library he ran brilliantly, and the books balanced within a month.
